newsitem.title: USA: CVS, Revco confirm merger talks.
newsitem.headline: CVS, Revco confirm merger talks.

text.p: CVS Corp. and Revco D.S. Inc. said Monday they were discussing a merger between the two drugstore giants.

The companies did not elaborate on any potential terms and warned the deal might not come to fruition. Revco, the second largest U.S. drugstore chain, and No. 5 CVS said neither would comment further until a deal is reached or the talks are terminated.

Nationally, Twinsburg, Ohio-based Revco is second only to Rite Aid Corp. in number of stores, with 2,600 drugstores in 17 states, mainly in the eastern United States, and home health care stores. The company rang up sales of about $5.08 billion in the 12 months ended June 1.

CVS, based in Woonsocket, R.I., is the fifth largest drugstore chain in terms of number of stores, with 1,408 outlets in 15 Northeastern and Middle Atlantic states and the District of Columbia. It had sales of about $9.7 billion in 1995.
The CVS-Revco combination is almost certain to draw heavy scrutiny from the Federal Trade Commission and other federal regulatory agencies.
CVS also will need to woo Revco Vice Chairman Sam Zell, whose Zell/Chilmark Fund LP owns about 20 percent of Revco stock.

If successful, the acquisition by CVS would mark a sharp reversal of roles for Revco, which is still smarting from the antitrust rejection of its attempt to buy out Rite Aid and is still settling in with its acquisition of Big B Inc.
CVS stock dropped 50 cents to $42.50 and Revco's dipped 37.5 cents to $38.875, both in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
